Subject: Security questionnaire — topology, segmentation, and attack-path walkthrough

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement review we need a compact packet that explains how Redwood fences tenant workloads and how lateral movement is prevented across zones. Specifically we need:  

- A network/topology diagram showing VPCs, subnets, sidecar placement, control-plane boundaries, and egress choke points
- A short narrative (one page) describing the isolation model and where a tenant process can and cannot send traffic
- A worked attack-path example (adversary starts from a tenant container -> attempts to exfiltrate to internet via shared egress) showing detection and mitigation controls
- Any firewall rules or sidecar ACL examples you can share (sanitized)

Can you get the packet to us by EOD Friday (Nov 27)? If you prefer, a short recorded walkthrough + artifacts is fine.

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Senior Security Engineer — HarborBank
security@harborbank.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — topology, segmentation, and attack-path walkthrough

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (network/runs) and Marissa (compliance) to assemble the packet. We can deliver the artifacts Friday; below is a short summary of what we will include and the single-page narrative:  

1) What you'll get (attachments): zonal-firebreak-diagram.svg (visual), attack-lattice-summary.pdf (1-page narrative + attack path), fw-rules-sample.txt (sanitized rule examples).

2) Isolation model (one-liner): Redwood enforces a layered fencing approach — tenant inference instances are colocated in tenant-specific compute pools with enforced VPC segmentation, enforced network policy at sidecar layer, control-plane endpoints on a separate management VPC accessible only via mutual-TLS and signed control tokens.

3) Key controls called out in the packet:
   - Zonal firebreaks: per-zone subnet ACLs + enforced egress proxies (no direct internet from tenant subnets)
   - Sidecar egress allowlisting: per-tenant allowlists and prefix-based caching to limit outbound destinations
   - Control plane separation: control traffic uses an isolated management fabric with HSM-backed keys and per-request signatures
   - Telemetry + detection: per-request tracing, token lineage, and anomaly scoring that triggers circuit-breaker and rollback on suspicious flows

We'll attach the diagram and the attack-lattice narrative; Karthik will add sample ACLs. If HarborBank would like a short recorded walkthrough, say 20 minutes, we can schedule on Friday afternoon.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Attachments: zonal-firebreak-diagram.svg (diagram), attack-lattice-summary.pdf (narrative)

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — topology, segmentation, and attack-path walkthrough

Jordan / Marissa — draft attachments are attached. Notes on the attack-path example in attack-lattice-summary.pdf:

- Step 1 (initial foothold): tenant workload compromise is limited to that tenant's compute pool. We show token lineage detection that tags abnormal L7 requests.
- Step 2 (lateral attempt): egress is forced through an instrumented proxy in a separate egress subnet; proxy enforces per-tenant allowlist and TLS inspection. We include sample iptables/ACL examples in fw-rules-sample.txt for the egress subnet.
- Step 3 (exfiltration attempt): outbound destinations that are not in the allowlist are blocked at the egress proxy; attempts trigger alerting and automated circuit-breaker that revokes session keys and quarantines the tenant instance.

Operational caveats to call out for HarborBank:
- Cross-zone replication happens over encrypted, authenticated tunnels between dedicated replication endpoints; tenant traffic is never used as a replication channel.
- Admin access to management VPC is via bastionless ephemeral sessions with KMS-backed signatures — we provide audit proofs for all session ops.

I sanitized the ACLs to remove internal IPs and left placeholders (TENANT_EGRESS_PROXY_IP).

Attached: fw-rules-sample.txt

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

2) For the egress proxy, do you have evidence of replayed flow captures (pcap-equivalent sanitized) or logs we can review? A short sampled log is fine.

If you can drop those two artifacts (timeline + sample proxy log) into the Drive link and reply here with the link by EOD, we'll consider this complete.

Best,
Alice
